name: portfolio
description: The periodic close of a portfolio under management: the third workload definition, and the second worked example's. Unit types are the steps of a close; each names the profile it runs under and the checks the host runs on its output — the portfolio's own test suite, run by the orchestrator, is the arithmetic. Two of them run a program rather than a session (#122): the rebalance plan and the harvest candidates are arithmetic over the tree, written under trades/proposed/ and checked by the host like a model's work. Nothing here trades: a trade list is a file a person executes at the custodian, written under trades/pending/ only after consent on every trade in it, by a session that asks.

unitTypes.name: ingest-positions
unitTypes.description: Bring the tax-lot ledger up to date with the fills the person recorded, reconciled to the custodian's latest export, and write the period review: the valuation, the time-weighted return, the open items. The custodian's exports and the fills are never edited.

unitTypes.name: propose-target
unitTypes.description: Write the period's target weights under targets/, with the band a rebalance lands inside. The target is feasible by the host's run of the portfolio's checks — long-only, summing to one, inside every benchmark subset's tolerance — not by the unit's say-so.

unitTypes.name: plan-rebalance
unitTypes.description: Compute the trade list that moves every targeted position toward the latest target at the latest export's prices, from the lots in the tax ordering and never through a wash sale, and write it under trades/proposed/ as a list a program computed and nobody has agreed to. A program, not a session (#122): the arithmetic is the workload's own, run by the control plane under a wall-clock budget, and the host checks the list it wrote exactly as it checks a model's. Consent and the copy under trades/pending/ are confirm-trades's.

unitTypes.name: confirm-trades
unitTypes.description: Put the proposed trade list to a person — one consent question naming every trade, the lots each sell comes from and the tax it realises — and, after the yes, write it unchanged under trades/pending/, where a file is a commitment. A session: it asks, which a program cannot. The host checks that the pending list is the proposed one and that it keeps the band, the lots and the wash-sale window.

unitTypes.name: harvest-losses
unitTypes.description: Find every open lot at an unrealised loss at the latest export's prices and write the candidates, with the loss per lot, under trades/proposed/ as harvest-<date>.json. A program, not a session (#122), with no threshold and no benefit-versus-cost judgment: that arithmetic, and turning a candidate into a sell with a replacement from its exchangeable set, is the harvest contract's (#124). The host checks every candidate against the lots and the prices.

unitTypes.name: review
unitTypes.description: Read the period's lots, target, proposed and pending trade lists, harvest candidates and review against the custodian's exports and say what does not agree. Read-only: it reports, and the host's run of the portfolio's checks is the evidence.

unitTypes.name: close-period
unitTypes.description: Confirm the period's evidence is fresh and its open items are dispositioned. Read-only.

metrics.name: workload:portfolio/turnover
metrics.description: The one-way turnover the latest target implies against the custodian's latest positions, at that export's prices: half the sum over the target's tickers of the absolute gap between the target weight and the current one, the fraction of the portfolio a rebalance to the target would trade. Lower is cheaper: every dollar traded is a spread paid and, on a sell, a gain realised. Measured by the workload's own grader over the tree (lib/portfolio.js's turnover), never from a unit's report.
